products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory, also called Shanghai AI Lab, is a non-profit government laboratory in China. Its website describes recruitment across large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, foundational platforms, innovation chain, and management support. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, including Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

The lab presents several releases under the Shusheng name. At the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum, it launched an upgraded scientific discovery platform called Shusheng Duanyan and opened its full-stack services, described as combining computation, proof, and verification. It also released the Shusheng physical world model W0 and the Shusheng embodied full-stack engine Intern-Robotics, which the lab says addresses data, training, and real-world application for embodied intelligence. At the 2026 WAIC Science Frontier Forum, the lab and partners released ten joint innovation results covering life sciences, materials science, and deep space astronomy. Professor Zhou Bowen is quoted proposing that scientific research is the next programming and that AI and science will drive each other.

InternLM, a product associated with the lab, is described as a Chinese open-source large language model tied to academic research. The lab also describes an AI-45 degree balance law, under which AI safety and performance should develop along a 45-degree line, and a risk management approach covering evaluation, training, base models, applications, and verification.
